$comment: One deployment of CircleChat and the Recursica agents. Copy to $CC_DIR/site.json (outside
any repository) and fill it in. Secrets never go here: each stack's secrets live in the stack's
GitHub environment, and the secrets helper writes them on each computer (circlechat/README.md).
nodes: every machine that runs something. Add as many as you have. 'address' is how the
CONTROL node's containers reach that machine: a VPN/Tailscale address or name, or
host.docker.internal for the control machine itself.
exactly one node has "control": true. It runs CircleChat, the agents and the gateway.
Any machine can be the control node, a Mac or a PC of any size (Windows runs it through WSL).
servers: the model servers a node runs, each with its kind (ollama, or mlx-lm on a Mac), its port
and the models it serves. Each model records memory_gb, the memory it needs. Every listed model
stays loaded, so the models must fit model_memory_gb, the memory the node gives its models.
mlx-lm serves one model: run one mlx-lm server, on its own port, for each model (a service).
An ollama server can set context_length, parallel and keep_alive, Ollama's own settings. On a Mac,
the kit's Ollama service on the control computer runs with them (circlechat/README.md, Model servers).
A model on an ollama server can set its own context_length and keep_alive, such as "10m", so the
model loads on its first request and unloads when idle. The gateway sends them with each request.
A model that can't think sets "thinking": false, and the gateway drops a request to think for it.
routes: a name agents ask for, mapped to an ordered list of backends. The gateway tries
them in order, so the last entry is the fallback. A backend is "<node>/<server id>/<model id>":
a route lists only the cluster's own models. A cloud model never joins a route.
An agent never names a model: it asks for a route by its role, such as coder, judge, general,
fast, reasoning or vision, and this file maps each route to models. Porter's port jobs ask for coder.
jobs: a node with a jobs block runs a job runner (circlechat/jobd) for long, heavy agent work,
such as Porter's adapter ports. Each job gets memory_gb of memory at most; slots jobs run at once.
porter: the release Porter watches, the adapters it ports to, and who it mentions with a result.
site.tenant, site.kind, site.preview_port, site.gateway_port, site.docker_context: one stack per
client on a shared computer. Leave them out for a single stack. A client or demo stack sets kind "client"
or "demo", its own tenant name and ports, and its own Docker VM; see circlechat/README.md, "Clients".
site.gateway_local_port: the gateway's agents' port on 127.0.0.1, for a RecursicaChat 2.0 server on
the control computer. Only the cluster's own stack sets it; see circlechat/README.md, "What reaches the gateway".
recursicachat: the RecursicaChat 2.0 server on the control computer. circlechat/rc-sync.sh sets each
agent's instructions, model, autonomy, sandbox and monthly budget there, at setup and hourly.
The sync uses the server's root-only CLI, and needs no account. agents.<handle>.recursicachat: the agent's model there,
one of the agent's routes, and budget_usd, a monthly budget in US dollars. See circlechat/README.md,
"Agents on RecursicaChat 2.0". For example: "recursicachat": {
"vault_key_file": "/etc/recursicachat/master.key"}, and in agents.loki: "recursicachat": {"model":
"local-small", "budget_usd": 5}: the model is one of the agent's routes, through the gateway
handle rc-loki and the provider gw-loki, which rc-sync.sh sets. Only the cluster's own stack sets either.
recursicachat.sessions: each program outside the server that uses its API as a member account, with
the account's email, the account that runs the program, and the file that holds its session. See
circlechat/README.md, "A session for a program outside the server".
recursicachat.services: each program that drives agents on the server, with the service's name, the
handles of the agents it drives, the account that runs the program, and the file that holds its
token. See circlechat/README.md, "A program that drives an agent". An entry with state may set
"health_report": true for each day's usage in <state>/usage/<day>/ and its note in the morning summary;
see circlechat/README.md, "A health report's usage export". kev_labels: the full path of the
folder where a review harness writes its Kev labels, the service account's own, mode 0750. Only the
cluster's own stack with data.repo sets it; see circlechat/README.md, "Kev's review data".
site.cloud_models.stall_minutes: how long a RecursicaChat task set to "Local, then cloud if significantly
delayed" waits for a first answer from the cluster before the gateway moves it to the cloud, 15 by default.
See circlechat/README.md, "Model use on RecursicaChat 2.0".
recursicachat.public_url, google_client_id and google_domain: the server's https address and its
Google sign-in, which circlechat/recursicachat/install.sh renders into the server's run.sh.
site.computers: the computers picked for a client or demo stack, ["<computer>"] or "cluster". The
stack's site.json lists only those computers; circlechat/kit/stack-site.mjs writes it from this file.
nodes[].limits: cpus, memory_gb and model_memory_gb for a picked computer, so a large computer acts
like a smaller one. A model that does not fit a stack's computers is left out, with a line that says so.
tailnet_address: the control node's Tailscale IP address. Port jobs on other nodes reach the
model gateway there.
slack_icon: an optional emoji for a node, such as :desktop_computer:. Each Slack message the
node's cluster programs post shows the node's name and this emoji as the sender. Slack shows
both only when the Slack app has the chat:write.customize scope.
router: an optional address of the router a node's default route must lead to. The network check
posts in Slack when the node's router differs. 192.0.2.1 is a placeholder: put the office router's
address there, or leave router out for no router check.
model_keys: the stack's cloud keys. Each named key records the provider, the cloud model and the
agents that use the key. The key's value lives only in the stack's GitHub environment, as
MODEL_KEY_<NAME> (MODEL_KEY_DEFAULT for the key named default). An agent no key names uses the
key named default. A task's "Cloud models" setting decides when a cloud key answers.
agents: each agent's routes (all routes when left out) and cloud switch (on when left out). A route
here can also name one cluster model, "<node>/<server id>/<model id>", to compare models. With
the switch off, the gateway never calls a cloud model for the agent.
notify.details: false leaves task titles and names out of the stack's Slack posts. Unset: on, except
for a client stack.
data.repo: a private repo for Kev's review data, the design reviews' Kev labels and Barb's notes, such as
your-org/recursica-kev-data. Each hour, new labels and notes go to a new branch there, with a pull request
for a person to review. Kev's training reads only what is merged into main, and only real-review labels.
Never the knowledge repo or a public repo: the push checks the repo's visibility first. Empty: no push. data.github_app: the push's own GitHub App,
with app_id, installation_id and slug, installed on data.repo only. The key is APP_KEY_KEV_DATA.
nodes[].rustdesk: the cluster's RustDesk Server Pro, on one Linux or WSL computer whose address is
its Tailscale IPv4 address: image (pinned by digest), console_host (the computer's Tailscale name)
and backup_time. The secret RUSTDESK_RESTIC_PASSWORD encrypts its backup. remote_access.direct_ip
false: every firewall refuses RustDesk's direct-address ports. See circlechat/README.md, "The RustDesk server".
knowledge: the knowledge MCP server on the control computer, the one way agents and programs read
the skills. The cluster's own stack only, so this example leaves the block out, like recursicachat:
"knowledge": { "port": 4011, "callers": [
{ "name": "example-harness", "account": "_example", "file": "/opt/example/run/knowledge.key" },
{ "name": "kev", "files": [{ "account": "_example", "file": "/opt/example/run/knowledge-kev.key" }] },
{ "name": "recursicachat", "agents": ["betty", "barb"], "builder": "agent-setup@example.com" } ] }
port: the server's port on 127.0.0.1. callers: each program that reads the skills, with its key
file: account and file, or files for a program that runs under several accounts, such as Kev. The
recursicachat caller's key stays with the kit: the agent sync registers the server on RecursicaChat
for the agents listed, signed in as the builder. See circlechat/README.md, "The knowledge MCP server".

services.name: kev-engine
services.command: uv run --no-sync --extra serve python -m kev.serve --run jaredpalmer/kev-4b --port 8009 --host 0.0.0.0
